correctness.rationale: Disjoint hub-pair determinant-fiber decomposition proves the exact target formula for every field and m. Each nonzero hub pair has an adapted unimodular basis and the resulting scalar equation has q, q^2 or 0 solutions as stated. The image and width conclusions follow from the support criterion and explicit decomposition, with a two-blade obstruction for m>=2. A standalone exhaustive checker confirmed every prescribed target in seven finite cases, normalization, and a separately computed conjugacy-count zero fiber. The finite check is not substituted for the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: Rossmann 2021 determines graphical conjugacy counts and therefore the zero commutator aggregate, which is prior and excluded from the original contribution. Naik 2018 and Cocke–Ho 2018 analyze commutator/word distributions generally but the inspected statements do not cover the complete friendship graphical-group nonzero fibers, image, and width boundary. Scientifically relevant published descriptions of two-generated class-two commuting graphs and finite Kronecker path algebra commutators concern different structures. Queries for equivalent graph/group/bivector terminology and exact image formulas yielded no decisive dominating source. Residual older-literature priority risk is reported; lack of hits is not itself the proof of originality.
residual_risks: Equivalent formulas might occur in older graph-group commutator-width or projected Grassmannian literature under different nomenclature.
Sinha, Commutators in Nilpotent Linear Groups of Class Two (1966), is a plausible broad antecedent; no full relevant article was accessible for a conclusive comparison.
Full independent verification of mathematical priority has not been performed.

value.rationale: For the natural commutator word map on an infinite family of finite graphical groups, this gives every nonzero target fiber, a complete support-structured image rather than just a global commuting probability, and the sharp structural commutator-width jump at two triangle blades. The image cardinality quantifies a genuine proper subset of the derived subgroup for m>=2 despite the derived subgroup being generated by commutators. All finite fields, including characteristic two, are covered.
